messages:
Ciara: Quick bring-up notes for komorebi-embed-compact on the holdout-10k suite. Ran fp16 vs int4 (symmetric quant, per-channel scaling). Summary: recall@1 ~= stable, recall@10 -6.2% on long-tail queries, cluster purity -0.08, silhouette -0.12. Dumping nearest-neighbor mismatches now. :eyes:

Sam: can you paste the top-line recall table?

Ciara: Sure — small table below (k=1/5/10):
```
model              | r@1   | r@5   | r@10
komorebi-fp16      | 0.724 | 0.842 | 0.873
komorebi-int4      | 0.718 | 0.800 | 0.811
delta (int4 - fp16)| -0.006| -0.042| -0.062
```

Jo: Oof r@10 drop is kind of large. Is this consistent across segments or concentrated?

Ciara: It's concentrated on long-tail (queries freq <= 5). Head queries look fine. Also multilingual short queries (fr, ja) see bigger regressions.

Anya: Did you run with prefix/KV cache enabled? Sometimes caching changes distribution for short queries.

Ciara: cache disabled for this run to avoid masking. Batch-size small (bs=64) — used runtime backend: our in-house vector runtime -> quant path.

Matt: Any sign of norm collapse? int4 symmetric sometimes reduces embedding norms, which affects cosine ranking. Can you print mean L2 per shard?

Ciara: Posted a quick sample: mean L2 (fp16) = 8.9, mean L2 (int4) = 6.1. Looks like scale shrinkage.

eval-bot: Automated eval summary: precision@10: fp16=0.873, int4=0.811; silhouette_score: fp16=0.34, int4=0.22; cluster_purity: fp16=0.61, int4=0.53. See /evals/1745005432/report.html

Sam: Useful. Hypotheses: a) per-channel scaling not correctly applied at inference path b) symmetric quantization zero-centers scales causing dot-product bias c) allocator/buffer alignment bug during runtime reorder.

Jo: To triage: 1) rerun int4 with per-dim affine (if available) 2) run dot-product rescaling (divide by scale) at query time 3) try ONNX-quant vs our runtime to see if it's runtime specific.

Ciara: I'll kick a quick job: python eval/recall.py --model komorebi-compact --quant int4 --quant-mode per-channel-affine --k 10 --segment longtail --backend onnx

Anya: Also add whitening/length-normalization ablation: sometimes int compresses variance and whitening recovers recall.

Matt: Could also be tokenization drift for short multilingual queries — embeddings upstream differ. Any raw-text diffs?

Ciara: Checked token counts, they match. Example mismatch (query + nearest in fp16 vs int4):
```
Query: "How do I reset my API key?"
fp16 top1: "Reset API key via Console > Tokens"
int4 top1: "Manage tokens in Console"
fp16 top10 includes exact doc, int4 missing it entirely in top10 for several queries.
```

Sam: If int4 removes the exact doc, likely dot-product magnitude changed relative order. Try re-scaling embeddings by inverse of quant scale per vector and re-eval (cheap offline).

Ciara: On it. Spawning three runs (affine, rescale, whitening) with longtail focus. Will report back in this thread.

eval-bot: New job queued 1745005472: komorebi-int4-affine-longtail (ETA ~18m).

Jo: If affine fixes it, we should gate int4 rollout by segment-level SLOs (longtail r@10 delta <= 2%). Should also add an automated per-segment comparator in Optimize that flags shortages. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Anya: Agreed. Also add an example set (20 queries) to the regression suite that captures this failure mode — include FR/JA short queries + API-key-like documentation queries.

Ciara: Added ticket ML-1189 to capture the regression test plus a small canary in prod. If affine doesn't help I'll revert to fp16 for dedicated customers and keep int4 as opt-in.

Matt: Thanks — ping here when jobs finish. If anyone else wants to look at the NN diffs I uploaded them to /tmp/komorebi_nn_mismatches.tar.gz

Sam: I'll check the diffs, leaving notes in the ticket. Good catch. :thumbsup:
